messages:
acme-bob: Hey team — hitting a recurring issue when we use the streaming endpoint. Client gets a broken pipe or ECONNRESET after ~10–30s and our dashboard shows a 5xx spike. Can you help?

maya: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a sample request id/trace and approximate timestamps? are you using our hosted API or Dedicated? :thinking_face:

acme-bob: hosted. trace id: trace_20260315_ab12f. Seen around 2026-03-15 15:12:30 UTC. Client stack is Node fetch() streaming the response and then closing the socket intermittently (we close early if user navigates away). Logs show:

```
2026-03-15T15:12:31Z gateway INFO request=start id=trace_20260315_ab12f route=/v1/streams
2026-03-15T15:12:35Z upstream WARN write error: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.0.18:52344: write: broken pipe
2026-03-15T15:12:35Z gateway ERROR response=502 id=trace_20260315_ab12f
```

acme-bob: Looks like the gateway logs a 502 when client disconnects during streaming. But from our perspective it was a client cancel, not a server error. We're getting billed for retries because we see 5xx in metrics.

jeff: @maya fyi — this smells like client disconnects being classified as 5xx upstream. Is the gateway counting any upstream write failure as a 5xx? We used to map client disconnects -> 499-like and not treat as server errors in metrics.

maya: filing repro now. acme-bob — can you share a minimal repro curl/node example that reproduces quickly? Also are you seeing this across multiple regions?

acme-bob: repro below (Node):

```
// run once: node repro-close.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const req = fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({prompt: 'x'.repeat(2000)}) });
setTimeout(() => {
  // simulate user navigating away
  req.body && req.body.destroy && req.body.destroy();
  console.log('client closed connection');
}, 12000);
```

acme-bob: After client closes we sometimes see 502 in the dashboard. Happy to share a HAR if useful.

ops-bot: alert: stream-error-rate has crossed 1% in us-west1 for the last 5m (inc: 176 alerts).

linh: pinging eng-runtime. cc @jeff. Can you paste the full gateway stack? Are we using Envoy/nginx or a custom proxy for streaming?

jeff: We're on our custom gateway with an nginx-ish reverse proxy layer + grpc/HTTP proxying. Historically the proxy converted EPIPE/EINVAL on write to upstream errors and returned a 502. We had a change last quarter that simplified error handling — might have regressed mapping.

linh: ok. hypoth: client TCP FIN / reset causes write(2) on socket to return EPIPE, and our proxy treats any write failure as upstream error. We should map EPIPE/EPIPE-like to client disconnect and return 499 (or at least not increment 5xx counter). Steps I'm taking: 1) reproduce locally with a short stream and kill client socket; 2) add extra logging to the gateway to log 'peer_closed' vs 'upstream_fault'; 3) patch telemetry to exclude 'peer_closed' from 5xx metric.

maya: timeline/ownership? acme-bob needs mitigation ASAP (they're flagged for overage).

linh: priority P1 for metrics correctness. Quick mitigation: change gateway to return 200 with truncated stream if upstream success but client closed? hmm not possible. Better: don't increment server 5xx metric when we detect write EPIPE. I can push a hotfix to change metric classification in the proxy (no functional behavior change). ETA 6 hours to roll small config.

jeff: +1. Also we should add a counter for 'client_disconnect_during_stream' and emit traces annotated with 'socket_state=client_closed' so support can filter.

acme-bob: Thanks — will that stop the billing/alert churn? We're charged per-request in hosted. If metrics don't count it as a 5xx, our automated billing rules won't trigger retries.

maya: short term: I'll mute the alert policy for the stream-error-rate in us-west1 until the fix is validated, to reduce noise. Long term: we'll fix metric classification and add a customer-visible FAQ about client-aborted streams (suggested client behavior: send FIN only after stopping read, or use explicit cancellation API).

linh: repro steps I used to validate locally (sharing so you can reproduce):
1) Start a small express server that streams chunked responses every second.
2) Use `curl -N` to start streaming and `kill -9` the curl process after 10s to cause abrupt disconnect.
3) Watch gateway logs for 'write error: broken pipe' and metrics increment.

Example curl repro:
```
# start streaming
curl -N -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
# kill process after 10s
sleep 10; kill -9 $!
```

linh: patch diff I'm going to apply (conceptual):
```
- if (upstream_write_failed) metric.increment('5xx')
+ if (upstream_write_failed && !is_client_disconnect(errno)) metric.increment('5xx')
```
Where is_client_disconnect checks EPIPE/ECONNRESET and TCP_RST flags.

jeff: make sure to update the aggregation rule that backs the '5xx' dashboard (remove counts where reason==client_disconnect) and add a filter in billing pipeline so we don't mark those for retry credits.

maya: action items:
- lin h: patch gateway classification and add client_disconnect metric (owner: linh) — ETA 6h
- jeff: update aggregation and billing filter + add alert filter (owner: jeff) — ETA 12h
- maya: mute noisy alert and message acme-bob with temporary guidance — ETA 30m

acme-bob: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. One request: can you add a note in the support ticket explaining whether retry behavior is influenced? Some clients retry on 5xx and we want to avoid double-cost.

maya: yes, will include that. Also adding a quick repro deck to the ticket: links and curl/node examples.

ops-bot: incident-note: ticket SUPPORT-12432 created (priority P1) assigned to eng-runtime.

linh: I'll post a follow-up here after the hotfix is rolled and we validate on us-west1 with the customer's repro.

maya: thanks everyone. acme-bob — expect an update in ~6 hours, ping me if this is urgent sooner. :thumbsup:
